trailheadDirection: From Leavenworth, drive US-2 west 0.8 mile, turn left onto Icicle Road for about 8.5 miles, then turn left onto Eightmile Road (FR-7600), stay right onto FR-7601 and follow it about 4 miles to the trailhead. The last stretch closes in winter, typically November to May.
approach: From the Stuart Lake Trailhead, follow the Stuart Lake trail about 2.5 miles to the split, then bear left on the Colchuck Lake trail for roughly 1.6 miles to Colchuck Lake. The route climbs the north face of Dragontail rising above the lake, starting on steep snow just left of the toe of the North Buttress.
note: Route page gives start (north face above Colchuck Lake, left of buttress toe); trail distances from peak page; no page describes the lake-to-base walk

trailheadDirection: From Leavenworth, drive US-2 west 0.8 mile, turn left onto Icicle Road for about 8.5 miles, then turn left onto Eightmile Road (FR-7600), stay right onto FR-7601 and follow it about 4 miles to the trailhead. The last stretch closes in winter, typically November to May.
approach: From the Stuart Lake Trailhead, follow the Stuart Lake trail about 2.5 miles to the split, then bear left on the Colchuck Lake trail for roughly 1.6 miles to Colchuck Lake. Continue up the Colchuck Glacier to Colchuck Col, where the route begins; a snow gully on the peak's south side leads from there to the summit ridge.
note: Route page (starts at Colchuck Col over the glacier, snow gully on south side) plus peak page trail distances; drive from sibling routes

trailheadDirection: From the Nisqually entrance of Mount Rainier National Park, drive east on Paradise Road through Longmire about 19 miles to the Paradise parking area. From November 1 through winter the road above Longmire closes nightly.
approach: From Paradise, work across toward the Kautz side, cross the lower Kautz Glacier and climb the Kautz Cleaver. Traverse from the cleaver into the easternmost Success Couloir, where the climb begins on steep snow.
note: Route page names Paradise / Van Trump / Westside Road as access and the cleaver traverse; no trail detail fetched. Mowich road closed, not used
previousSecondCheck: corrected: Deleted unsupported 'easternmost couloir' claim; Kautz-side approach only partly backed; drive closure updated to NPS Oct 28 2026 status. | hand: gate stated as the yearly pattern, not one date

trailheadDirection: From I-90 exit 85 take SR-970 east 7 miles, turn left onto Teanaway Road, and after 7.1 miles bear right onto North Fork Teanaway Road. Where the pavement ends after 5.9 miles take the right fork onto FR-9737 and continue about 9.5 miles, keeping left at the Beverly Campground fork and right at the fork for the trailhead, to the parking area.
approach: From the Esmeralda Basin Trailhead (FR-9737), follow the old mine road about 0.25 mile to a fork and turn right onto the Ingalls Way trail. Hike roughly 3 miles to Ingalls Pass and on to Ingalls Lake, about 4 miles from the car. Scramble to the notch between the north and south summits, then drop west about 100 feet to a friction slab, where the Southwest Face begins.
note: Club route page covers the Southwest Face start at the notch on the main (north) summit; drive from sibling

trailheadDirection: From Leavenworth, drive US-2 west 0.8 mile, turn left onto Icicle Road for about 8.5 miles, then turn left onto Eightmile Road (FR-7600), stay right onto FR-7601 and follow it about 4 miles to the trailhead. The last stretch closes in winter, typically November to May.
approach: From the Stuart Lake Trailhead (Trail #1599), follow the Stuart Lake trail about 3 miles to the south branch of Mountaineer Creek. A climber's path may lead up that creek from the west edge of the big swamp near 4600 ft; follow the drainage about 2 miles to the head of the valley near 5800 ft. Turn west and climb roughly half a mile to the base of the Northeast Face.
note: Peak page north approaches: base of North Ridge or Northeast Face; page admits it has not seen these routes; drive from sibling routes

trailheadDirection: Leave I-90 at Exit 62 for Kachess Lake, follow the signs about 5 miles to Kachess Lake Campground, then turn left onto Box Canyon Road (FR 4930) and go 4.2 miles to the parking at the Rachel Lake Trailhead.
approach: From the Rachel Lake Trailhead, walk the Rachel Lake trail to about 3300 ft, where a brushy clearing shows the summit. Enter the forest there and climb the steep boot path northeast, keeping right at a small clearing after roughly 500 ft of gain. Pass the rock band near 5300 ft on its right, cross the sloping meadow and aim for the right-hand (south) side of the summit block through loose talus; the climbing starts at the south side of the block.
note: Mountaineers Hibox page (browser, cached) describes the standard line to the south side of the summit block; matched to South Route by that geometry, not name alone
previousSecondCheck: rejected: The blog describes one standard hike up the trail path and talus; no page I opened ties it to the South Route, and reports show a separate southeast-ridge line off the trail further in. Cannot back that this reaches this route's base.

trailheadDirection: From US 2 just past the Skykomish Ranger Station, turn south onto Foss River Road (FR 68) and drive about 4 miles to the Necklace Valley Trailhead parking on the left.
approach: From the Necklace Valley Trailhead, follow the Necklace Valley Trail up the East Fork Foss River, over the river crossing and the steep climb beyond it, to the hanging valley holding La Bohn Lakes, where parties camp. From the lakes, climb the snow chute or talus to La Bohn Gap; the climb proper heads due north from the gap toward the summit.
note: Mountaineers West Route page (browser, cached) + WTA Necklace Valley page agree
previousSecondCheck: rejected: Only page opened calls La Bohn route the "standard route"; no opened page ties it to the West Route (mountaineers.org/SummitPost 403).

trailheadDirection: From I-90 Exit 34 near North Bend, drive north on 468th Ave SE, turn right onto SE Middle Fork Road (which becomes FR 56) and follow it to the Middle Fork Snoqualmie Trailhead at the end.
approach: From the Middle Fork Snoqualmie Trailhead, cross the river bridge and turn west onto the Pratt Connector Trail, then take the unofficial Rainy Creek path up to Rainy Lake at about 3800 ft. From the lake, climb the ridge to the east in a clockwise sweep to a tarn at 5200 ft, then head south onto a ridge leading to a saddle near 5800 ft. From that saddle a short ridge walk runs south to the summit, so the north-side route begins there.
note: Mountaineers Preacher page (browser, cached): the only described line reaches the summit from the north via the 5800 ft saddle; matched to North Route by direction, not name alone
